facts.statement: Asiaceratops was a herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur whose name means "Asian horned face".
facts.quote: Asiaceratops (meaning "Asian horned face") is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur.

facts.statement: The type species A. salsopaludalis is found in Uzbekistan, while the second species A. sulcidens is found in China and Mongolia.
facts.quote: The type species, A. salsopaludalis is known from Uzbekistan, while A. sulcidens is known from China and Mongolia.

facts.statement: Asiaceratops salsopaludalis was formally described by Nesov, Kaznyshkina, and Cherepanov in 1989.
facts.quote: The type species, Asiaceratops salsopaludalis, was formally described by Lev Nesov, L.F. Kaznyshkina and Gennadiy Olegovich Cherepanov in 1989.

facts.statement: The specific name salsopaludalis means "of the salt marsh" in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name means "of the salt marsh" in Latin.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a fragment of a left maxilla.
facts.quote: It consists of a part of a left maxilla.

facts.statement: In 1995, Nesov referred additional material from three Uzbek sites, including mostly skull elements and a partial humerus.
facts.quote: In 1995 Nesov referred more material, from three Uzbek sites, mostly skull elements and a partial humerus, of individuals of different ages.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses indicate a basal position for Asiaceratops within the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Recent cladistic analyses indicated, despite the presumed status as a nomen dubium, a basal position in the Leptoceratopsidae.

facts.statement: More recent phylogenetic analyses consistently place Asiaceratops as a basal neoceratopsian outside the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: More recent phylogenetic analyses consistently recover Asiaceratops as a basal neoceratopsian outside Leptoceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Because flowering plants were limited during the Cretaceous, Asiaceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: During the Cretaceous, flowering plants were "geographically limited on the landscape", and so it is likely that this dinosaur fed on the predominant plants of the era: ferns, cycads, and conifers.

facts.statement: Asiaceratops used its sharp beak to bite off leaves or needles.
facts.quote: It would have used its sharp ceratopsian beak to bite off the leaves or needles.

facts.statement: Asiaceratops lived during the Early to Late Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: It lived during the Early-Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Asiaceratops salsopaludalis lived in the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous, about 99 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 99 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Asiaceratops is the Cenomanian, spanning from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Asiaceratops is a valid taxon, as it has often been considered a nomen dubium due to limited material.
facts.quote: Asiaceratops has often been considered a nomen dubium, in view of the limited holotype material.
